calls.body: The Ducks played last night and get no rest before this one. Teams in that spot usually get the worse of the chances, so we expect the Flames to control more of the play than they usually do.

surprises.head: Calgary’s power play hit a new low
surprises.body: Calgary has one of the league’s least dangerous power plays. Even by those standards, this was a dry night: 1.6 expected goals per 60 on the power play, against their usual 6.6 and a league average of 7.6. A team strays this far about once every 25 games.

story.head: The Ducks beat the Flames
paras: The Ducks’ Cutter Gauthier left in the first period and didn’t return. Jackson LaCombe got the scoring started for the Ducks on the power play midway through the first. Morgan Frost tied it late in the first. Frank Vatrano gave the Ducks the lead 4:12 later. Calgary had a goal taken off for offside midway through the second. Aydar Suniev, in his ninth NHL game, scored his first NHL goal, set up by Matt Coronato, late in the second to tie it 2-2. Ryan Poehling put the Ducks ahead for good shorthanded early in the third. Nikita Nesterenko added insurance with 2:57 left.

Nothing much separated these two on the chances. This one could have gone either way. Ville Husso made 27 saves for the Ducks, and Dustin Wolf stopped 24 of 28. By our Swing measure, Alex Killorn had the best night of anyone. The Ducks improved to 4-1-0.

items.text: The Flames are 0-5-0, still looking for their first win.
Joel Farabee’s five-game point streak against Anaheim ended.
Ryan Poehling scored his first goal of the season, his first since Apr 3 (ten games played since).
Both of the preview’s calls held.
